places.name: Persepolis
places.summary: Ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire; inscribed by UNESCO in 1979.

facts.t: Inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1979.
Venue for part of the October 1971 celebrations of 2,500 years of the Iranian monarchy; they opened on 12 October at the tomb of Cyrus at Pasargadae.

places.name: Golestan Palace
places.summary: Qajar-era royal complex in the historic core of Tehran.

facts.t: Originally built in the Safavid period; took its most characteristic form in the 19th century as the Qajar family's royal residence and seat of power.
Inscribed on the World Heritage List on 23 June 2013.

places.name: Trans-Iranian Railway
places.summary: 1,394 km standard-gauge line opened fully in 1938.

facts.t: Connects the Caspian Sea in the north to the Persian Gulf in the south; opened fully in 1938.
Inscribed on the World Heritage List on 25 July 2021.
Built during Reza Shah's reign as part of the expansion of roads, railways and state factories.

places.name: University of Tehran
places.summary: Iran's first university, inaugurated on 4 February 1935 under a law introduced in 1934.

facts.t: A law establishing the university was introduced in the Majlis on 13 March 1934; the university was inaugurated on 4 February 1935.
The Library of Congress gives 1935 for its establishment as the first European-style university.

places.name: Azadi (Shahyad) Tower
places.summary: Marble-clad monument inaugurated in October 1971, designed by Hossein Amanat.

facts.t: Designed by Hossein Amanat, whose entry was chosen in a national competition announced in September 1966; originally the Shahyad Aryamehr Monument, renamed Azadi after 1979.
Inaugurated at sunset on 16 October 1971 as part of the celebrations (one thesis, citing the contemporary press; other accounts may give 17 October).

places.name: Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art
places.summary: Museum inaugurated in 1977 and designed by Kamran Diba.

facts.t: Inaugurated by Farah Pahlavi in 1977; designed by Kamran Diba.
The architect dates the project 1967-1976 and was interim director for eighteen months after completion.
